Rule: A.1 item 25 'COBOL character repertoire (encoding of, mapping of, substitute graphics) ... required ... documented (8.1.3; 8.1.3 GR1 and 5)'. cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 "The implementor shall define a mapping of each basic letter, basic digit, basic special character, and extended letter" -> OK §8.1.3.2 1) (General rules). cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 "substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented" -> OK §8.1.3.2 5). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 "Character-1 may be any character in the coded character set that the implementor has chosen for source code representation" -> OK §8.3.3.2.3 2) (Syntax rules). Determination reasoning: ISO leaves the mapping and the source encoding to the implementor (GR1) but a literal may hold only characters of the chosen source set (8.3.3.2.3 SR2); U+FFFD substitution silently changes a literal's content, so it is not a choice to document (PB1535). Two candidate fixes were on the table in PB1397 step 3 — a strict decoder with an error, or byte pass-through. Rule-1 precedence settles it: GnuCOBOL (next after ISO) accepts such source and preserves each byte as one character (no iconv on source), so rejecting it would be less conforming to the precedence than preserving it; in a UTF-16 repertoire the unique byte-preserving decoding is ISO/IEC 8859-1 (code point = byte, so FUNCTION ORD equals GnuCOBOL's byte+1 for every such byte). Whole-file (not per-sequence) fallback keeps DOC-A.1-26's one-encoding-per-file model; the warning keeps a CP1252 source (0x80 -> U+0080, not €) from being reinterpreted invisibly. PARTIAL: the ISO 10646/UTF-16 mapping and the BOM-selected encodings hold (DOC-A.1-26 probe, item 32/74 goldens); the malformed-UTF-8 arm diverges (probe). Owning defect kb/Work PB1397 (open, keeps DOC-A.1-25 per its step-3 section). The fix: CompilationInputs.ReadAllText detects BOM itself, decodes with UTF8Encoding(throwOnInvalidBytes: true), on DecoderFallbackException re-decodes the file as Latin-1 and records a warning (needs an allocated COBOLNET code). Witness needed: a golden reading a no-BOM file with a raw 0xE9 in a literal, expecting DISPLAY é and ORD 234 plus the warning in .err. Row stays GAP until then. No precedent: GnuCOBOL 3.2's >>DISPLAY has no UPON device (its lexer collects the words as text, per doc-rows-1's reading of cobc/pplex.l); IBM Enterprise COBOL and Micro Focus have no ISO DISPLAY directive.
